meta.title: Load Balancer: Realistic Use Cases
meta.subtitle: Portrait 9:16 layout of the same six jobs

components.label: Mobile Users
components.note: Traffic from the native mobile app. The load balancer routes these requests to a backend pool tuned for mobile payloads.

components.label: Desktop Users
components.note: Traffic from the desktop web app. Routed to a separate pool that serves full HTML pages instead of the mobile API responses.

components.label: Returning User
components.note: A user with an existing session cookie. The load balancer honors sticky sessions and pins their requests back to the same instance.

components.label: Health Checker
components.note: Periodically probes every backend instance. An instance that stops responding correctly is marked unhealthy and excluded from routing until it recovers.

components.label: Load Balancer
components.note: The central traffic distributor. Terminates inbound HTTPS, routes by platform, consults health status, and enforces session affinity before forwarding to a backend pool.

components.label: Mobile API Pool
components.note: A backend pool optimized for mobile API traffic: lighter payloads and endpoints tailored to the mobile app, backed by Zone A instances.

components.label: Session Store
components.note: Tracks which backend instance owns each session, so the load balancer can consistently pin a returning user to the same server instead of load-balancing them elsewhere.

components.label: Web App Pool
components.note: A backend pool that renders full web pages for the desktop app, backed by Zone B instances.

components.label: Instance A2
components.note: A healthy server instance in Availability Zone A, actively receiving traffic from the Mobile API Pool.

components.label: Instance A1
components.note: A healthy server instance in Availability Zone A. Currently pinned as the sticky-session target for returning users tracked in the Session Store.

components.label: Instance A3
components.note: Failed its last health probe. The load balancer has excluded it from rotation so no traffic reaches it until it passes a probe again.

components.label: Instance B1
components.note: A healthy server instance in Availability Zone B, serving full-page requests from the Web App Pool.

components.label: Instance B2
components.note: A healthy server instance in Availability Zone B, providing capacity in a second zone for resilience if Zone A degrades.

cards.title: Failure handling
items: Traffic is automatically redirected away from a malfunctioning instance (A3) to keep the service continuously available.

cards.title: Instance health checks
items: The load balancer continuously polls instance health and only routes to servers that report healthy.

cards.title: Platform-specific routing
items: Mobile and desktop requests are routed to specialized backend pools so each device type gets a tailored response.

cards.title: SSL termination
items: The load balancer decrypts inbound HTTPS traffic, offloading TLS work from backend instances.

cards.title: Cross-zone load balancing
items: Requests can be distributed across Availability Zone A and Zone B, improving resilience beyond a single zone.

cards.title: User stickiness
items: A returning user's requests are consistently pinned to the same backend instance to preserve session state.
